sourcedFrom: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 (2021)
cleanIntro: The short Nelson: 6.85 inches, 1.75 in diameter, 12.2 oz of titanium, direct thread 5/8-24 with no brake or adapter between it and the barrel. It is 2 inches shorter and about 12 dB louder than the Full Nelson on the same ammunition, and it takes the same two-way install torque decision. Q's sheet covers both cans together under the name Nelson Bros., so check which column your figures came from.

steps.title: Clear the host, bolt locked to the rear
steps.action: Magazine out, bolt locked back, then check the chamber and magazine well visually and with a finger before touching the can. Q names the locked-back bolt explicitly on this sheet, which matters on a short can that sits close to the ejection port.
steps.prose: A direct-thread can comes off with a hard twist. That is not something to do one-handed over a rifle you have not proved.
steps.quote: BEFORE REMOVING ANY SILENCER FROM ITS HOST, REMOVE THE MAGAZINE FROM YOUR FIREARM, MAKE SURE THE BOLT IS LOCKED TO THE REAR AND THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED BY PERFORMING A PHYSICAL AND VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE WELL.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — REMOVAL, p.1

steps.title: Read the FINE PRINT sheet as well as this one
steps.action: Q requires this sheet and the FINE PRINT sheet that ships with the can to be read together, and warns that failing to do so can result in property damage, serious injury or death. Neither sheet explains how to clear your rifle — that comes from the host firearm's own manual.
steps.prose: The sheet is a spec card with warnings on it. It is not an owner's manual and Q does not present it as one.
steps.caution: If the FINE PRINT sheet is not in the box, the instructions are incomplete.
steps.quote: BEFORE USING THIS SILENCER: BE CERTAIN YOU HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THIS MANUAL AND THE  ACCOMPANYING “FINE PRINT” SHEET.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — LAWYER SHIT, p.1

steps.title: Half Nelson ceiling — 7.62mm and smaller projectiles
steps.action: Match the host's bore to the rating before mounting. Q rates the Nelson Bros. for 7.62mm and smaller projectiles only, and the SPECS block carrying the Half Nelson's name lists 7.62 NATO, 300 BLK and 300 WM. This is a projectile diameter limit and applies whatever the chambering is called.
steps.prose: Your can's own figures are 6.85 in, 1.75 in and 12.2 oz, with 133 dB on 220gr 300 BLK from a 7 inch barrel and 140 dB on 175gr 7.62x51 from a 16 inch barrel. The quieter 121/130 dB column belongs to the longer Full Nelson.
steps.quote: THE NELSON BROS. ARE ONLY FOR USE WITH 7.62MM AND SMALLER PROJECTILES.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — LAWYER SHIT, p.1
steps.warn: 7.62mm is the ceiling. 140 dB on 7.62x51 means hearing protection stays on.

steps.title: Factory SAAMI or C.I.P. approved ammunition only
steps.action: Q limits this can to factory certified, SAAMI or C.I.P. approved ammunition. A direct-thread can has nothing between it and your barrel to correct for a badly behaved bullet, and the Half Nelson's shorter body puts the front cap closer to the muzzle than the Full Nelson's does.
steps.prose: Reloads and remanufactured ammunition are outside the specification. That is a warranty statement as well as a safety one.
steps.quote: ONLY USE FACTORY CERTIFIED SAAMI/C.I.P. APPROVED AMMUNITION WITH THIS SILENCER by Q.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — LAWYER SHIT, p.1

steps.title: Let the heat off before you handle it
steps.action: A short can absorbs the same gas volume into less metal, so the Half Nelson gets hot faster than its long brother. Q's instruction is to wait a minute before putting a finger anywhere near a just-fired chamber, and the can is in exactly the same state.
steps.prose: 12.2 oz of titanium at 6.85 inches has very little thermal mass. It will still be dangerous long after it stops glowing anywhere. The manual prints an ellipsis inside this sentence; the citation is cut to the contiguous side so nothing is elided by us. Its other half reads: "THAT SHIT GETS HOT.".
steps.quote: IF YOU JUST FINISHED SHOOTING, I’D WAIT A MINUTE BEFORE YOU STICK A FINGER IN THE CHAMBER
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — REMOVAL, p.1
steps.warn: Gloves or a cover if it cannot wait.

steps.title: Unthread the Half Nelson off the barrel
steps.action: Wrench on the 7/8 SAE flats at the rear and turn counter-clockwise. Q machines those flats into both Nelsons for install and removal, with a second 3/4 SAE set at the front for a can that ends up under a handguard. The removal is that one turn and nothing more.
steps.prose: On the Half Nelson the front flats are the ones you will reach for on a short handguard, so know both sizes before you start.
steps.caution: Load goes into the flats, never into the 1.75 in tube wall.
steps.quote: 3.Righty tighty. The Nelson Bros. feature 7/8 SAE ﬂats on the rear. We recommend you use these for install and removal. They also feature 3/4 SAE ﬂats on the front for silencers installed under a handguard. You’re welcome.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — INSTALLATION ONTO THE HOST FIREARM, p.1

steps.title: Square shoulder or tapered? That decides the reinstall torque
steps.action: The Half Nelson takes 25 to 30 ft-lbs on a SQUARE shoulder and only 10 to 15 ft-lbs on a TAPERED barrel. Establish which yours is before you pick a number: a square shoulder is a flat face perpendicular to the bore behind the threads, a tapered barrel runs a cone into them. Applying the square-shoulder figure to a taper crushes and galls the cone.
steps.prose: Q gives both numbers on one line of the sheet and leaves the choice with the owner, because only the owner can see the barrel.
steps.aside: Quoted as the extraction renders it — the ft ligature drops out of every 'ft-lbs' on this sheet. The alternative on the same line reads '10 to 15 -lbs on TAPERED barrel'.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — INSTALLATION ONTO THE HOST FIREARM, torque table, p.1
steps.warn: Two torque values, one can. The barrel decides, not the wrench.

steps.title: Clean the muzzle interface both sides
steps.action: With the can off, clean and degrease the barrel's taper or shoulder and its threads, then clean the matching features in the rear of the Half Nelson. Q names alignment as the reason: fouling on those faces cants the can relative to the bore axis, and the shorter the can the less forgiving that is.
steps.prose: Solvent-moistened Scotch-Brite or a brass or nylon brush. Steel tools are barred, and a scored taper never seats consistently again.
steps.caution: DO NOT USE STEEL TOOLS FOR CLEANING.
steps.quote: 3.At a minimum, it is also recommended to clean the barrel’s taper / shoulder and threads as well as the corresponding silencer features of any fouling. This will help with alignment of the silencer to the barrel’s axis, ensuring optimal performance.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.1

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The Half Nelson is off the barrel and that is the whole strip Q documents for it. The sheet has installation, removal and cleaning sections and no disassembly section at all — the tube is not designed to open. Internal cleaning, if it is wanted, is a copper solvent bath or an ultrasonic cycle with the can assembled, followed by complete drainage.
steps.prose: Q's stated view is that a centrefire rifle can does not need the attention a rimfire or a pistol can does, because the pressures and temperatures involved keep it clean.
steps.quote: 1.If you wish to clean this silencer, we recommend submerging it in a copper solvent or an ultrasonic cleaner.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.1
steps.warn: Fully drained before firing — no exceptions.

deepAbsentReason: Q PUBLISHES NO DISASSEMBLY FOR THE HALF NELSON. Its sheet contains no disassembly section; the REMOVAL section is two lines about unthreading the can from the barrel, and the deepest maintenance instruction is submerging the assembled can in copper solvent or an ultrasonic cleaner. No baffle count, no end-cap procedure and no internal torque appears anywhere in the document. Because Q's own EL CAMINO and ERECTOR sheets print full teardowns, the absence here is a fact about this product and not a gap in the paperwork. No deep clean is offered.

cleaning.name: BARREL INTERFACE
tasks: Clean and degrease the barrel's taper or shoulder and its 5/8-24 threads
Clean the matching seat and threads in the rear of the Half Nelson
Solvent-moistened Scotch-Brite or a brass or nylon brush — never steel
Confirm which shoulder type you have before choosing a reinstall torque

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR AND FLATS
tasks: Wipe the 7/8 SAE rear flats and the 3/4 SAE front flats clean
Inspect the 1.75 in tube for dents or bulging, especially near the front cap
Wear PPE — Q requires it for all firearms cleaning and maintenance

cleaning.name: INTERIOR (ASSEMBLED)
tasks: Submerge the assembled can in copper solvent, or run an ultrasonic cycle
Drain it completely before it goes anywhere near a muzzle
Do not try to open the tube; Q documents no way to do it

reassembly: Strip any muzzle device off the 5/8-24 barrel and clean and degrease the threads.
Start the Half Nelson by hand, clockwise, and feel that the thread has picked up straight.
Tighten on the 7/8 SAE rear flats to 25 to 30 ft-lbs on a SQUARE shoulder, or 10 to 15 ft-lbs on a TAPERED barrel.
Never carry one of those torque figures across to the other barrel geometry.
fncheck: With the Half Nelson torqued to the figure matching your barrel's shoulder, check it has drawn up tight against the shoulder with no gap and sits true to the bore. Sight down the tube and confirm the exit is round, central and unmarked. Direct-thread cans loosen under fire — check tightness again after the first few rounds.
